the reconstruction with percraniomuscular and fascia temporal flap has represented the ideal solution for reparation of the defect of cranial vault, radiation treated and under a multiplicitiy of surgical interventions for recidivism of neoplastic cutis, in the case of the patient presented in this study.
we have described an original technique for the treatment of the cranial osseous loss with a pericranial flap and a pedunculated temporalis muscle.
the pericranium is a very useful tissue for the reconstruction of cranial vault defects and that the temporal muscle is a good option for the reconstruction of the temporal bone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the temporalis muscle and fascia-pericrannial flap for the reconstruction of a loss of substance of the cranial bone.

the study of a clinical case of reconstruction of the loss of cranial vault substance, with exposure of the bone, through the use of pericranial and temporalis fascia flaps, pedunculizing the muscle flap.
the use of the pericardial muscle flap and fascia temporal for the coverage of loss of substance in the cranial region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the reconstruction of the loss of cranial vault substance with osseus exposure, through the use of the pericardial flap and the fascia temporalis pedunculated muscle flap, is an excellent alternative for the reparation and reconstruction of the craniofacial defect, especially in the case of the patient under the treatment for radiation and neoplastic recurrences.

the pericranium and the temporalis muscle, as well as the galea aponeurotica, are the most suitable flapping for the reconstruction of the skull, and the use of the temporalis muscle and the galea are the most appropriate flapping for the reparation and reconstruction of the skull vault.

the use of the pedunculated temporalis muscle flap, in association with pericranium and cutaneous grafts in the reparation of the cranial defect in a patient who has undergone a multiplicity of previous surgical interventions and radiation therapy, is a valid technique for the reconstruction of a cranial vault defect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of the cranial region, we must always try to use the local tissue, but when it is not enough or when the local flaps are not suitable, the revascularization of free flaps becomes fundamental.

the pericranium and temporalis fascia flaps can be considered an alternative to the use of free flaps in the treatment of cranial vault loss of substance, in particular in cases of irradiation, where the local flap has a higher rate of necrosis.

in the reconstruction of the loss of cranial substance, the use of the pericranius and the temporalis muscle, in the form of a pedunculated flap, is a valid alternative to other flaps described in the literature, which are more difficult and more expensive to perform, like the free flaps.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the reconstruction of the loss of the substance of the cranial bone with the pedunculate muscle flap and fascia temporal, in a radiation-treated patient with multiple surgical interventions and cutaneous neoplastic recidity, has been an ideal solution for the reconstruction of the bone loss of the cranial region.

in the case of a loss of substance of the cranial region, with the presence of an ulcerated cutis, the use of local tissue flaps, pedunculated, is a valid solution for the reconstruction of the defect.

the reconstruction of the loss of osseous substance from the cranial vault with pericranium, fascia temporal, and muscle flap is an alternative to the free flaps, which can be used in the reconstruction of the vault cranial in patients who have undergone radiation therapy and multiple surgeries for the treatment of neoplastic recurrences.
